series.description: 100% is a five-issue miniseries written and drawn by Paul Pope, published in black and white by DC's Vertigo imprint between 2002 and 2003. Set in a New York of 2038 and unfolding over two weeks, it follows six characters (Kim, Strel, Eloy, John, Daisy and Haitous) through interlocking romances staged among underground boxing and the neo-erotic gastro dancing revue, where performers dance with their stomachs lit from within. Collected as a trade paperback in 2005.

series.name: Absolute Martian Manhunter
series.description: Absolute Martian Manhunter is an abstract superhero psychological horror comic book maxiseries published by DC Comics, based on its character Martian Manhunter. The series is written by Deniz Camp and illustrated by Javier Rodríguez, and was released on March 26, 2025 as part of DC's Absolute Universe (AU) imprint. It is the fifth series from the imprint released in order, and is second in the second batch of Absolute titles, following Absolute Flash and continuing with Absolute Green Lantern.

series.name: Absolute Wonder Woman
series.description: Absolute Wonder Woman is a superhero series written by Kelly Thompson and illustrated by Hayden Sherman, published by DC Comics as part of its Absolute Universe imprint beginning in October 2024. It reimagines Diana as the last of the Amazons, taken as an infant and raised in Hell among monsters rather than on Themyscira, who makes her public debut when kaiju-scale Harbingers attack Gateway City.

series.name: Action Comics
series.description:
Continued in Action Comics Volume 2.

In the early days of comics books, it was not the convention to name comics after specific characters. Rather comics bore generic names such as this one. Although this series featured Superman throughout, it thus bore this name, one which it has become famous for (and the name was kept after the launch of The New 52.) It was the fourth DC Comics title, and the first new one produced after Detective Comics spread beyond the one title (this was after it purchased More Fun Comics and New Adventure Comics.) Originally an anthology series that featured several co-starring characters. As the page size of the series was reduced so to with the co-starring features. When Action Comics was reduced to 32 pages; it only contained one co-starring feature all the way up to the late Bronze Age. With the start of the Modern Age, Action Comics temporarily became a Superman team-up feature until issue #599.

series.name: Anubis
series.description:
Published from 1996 to 1997 with 7 total issues numbered 1-7.

Issues 1-3 published by SCC Entertainment, 4-5 published by Didactic Chocolate Press, and 6-7 published by Adventure Comics.

Issues 1-2 collected in Anubis.

series.name: Archie
series.description:
Archie Comics' flagship title, relaunched by Oni Press in 2026 under a new publishing partnership timed to the 85th anniversary of Archie Andrews' first appearance in Pep Comics #22. Written by Ben H. Winters with art by Fábio Moon, the ongoing follows a seventeen-year-old Archie through Riverdale's past, present, and future.

The extra-sized, 40-page first issue arrived September 2, 2026 with a main cover by Stuart Immonen and variants by Moon, Karl Kerschl, Khary Randolph, Kano, Dan Parent, Elsa Charretier and Mahmud Asrar, joined at final order cutoff by a surprise cover from Travis Charest. It leads a three-title line alongside Sabrina the Teenage Witch by Corinna Bechko and Kano, and Archie in Hell by Patrick Horvath and Tyler Crook.

series.name: Assorted Crisis Events
series.description: Assorted Crisis Events is an ongoing anthology series by writer Deniz Camp and artist Eric Zawadzki, with colorist Jordie Bellaire and letterer Hassan Otsmane-Elhaou, launched by Image Comics in March 2025. Each issue follows ordinary people caught inside an unexplained and ongoing crisis in time: commuters trapped in loops, cavemen and cyborg soldiers sharing a red-light district, Victorian debutantes puzzling over cell phone plans. Reviewers have described it as Crisis on Infinite Earths as experienced by everyday people, or Black Mirror with the fabric of space and time breaking down.

series.name: Avenue D
series.description: Avenue D is a black-and-white comics magazine written and drawn by Glenn Head and published by Fantagraphics Books, following a self-published first issue. Its semi-autobiographical vignettes take in punk-era life on New York's Lower East Side, with the recurring character Bob the Snowman. Head went on to co-edit the alternative anthology Snake Eyes with Kaz.

series.name: Battle Beast
series.description: Battle Beast, published as Invincible Universe: Battle Beast, is an ongoing series by writer Robert Kirkman and artist Ryan Ottley, the longtime Invincible creative team, launched by Image Comics and Skybound in April 2025. It tells the untold story of the fan-favorite Battle Beast, cursed with an unquenchable thirst for violence, as he ranges across the universe in search of an opponent worthy of him.

series.name: Beneath the Trees Where Nobody Sees: Rite of Spring
series.description: Beneath the Trees Where Nobody Sees: Rite of Spring is a six-issue sequel to Patrick Horvath's Eisner-nominated series, published by IDW Publishing in 2025. It is 1994, nearly a decade after the cuddly brown bear Samantha Strong made herself Woodbrook's only serial killer, and the arrival of the internet means there are no secrets left. Monica Brewer, a white duck who has spent eight years looking for her brother Daniel, follows an online tip to Woodbrook and asks for help from the very bear who killed him.

series.name: Bijou Funnies
series.description: Bijou Funnies was an American underground comix anthology that ran for eight issues between 1968 and 1973. Edited by Chicago cartoonist Jay Lynch, it grew out of the underground newspaper The Chicago Mirror and featured Lynch, Skip Williamson, Robert Crumb and Jay Kinney alongside contributors including Art Spiegelman, Gilbert Shelton, Justin Green and Kim Deitch. Heavily indebted to Mad, it is regarded alongside Zap as one of the titles that launched the underground comix movement. Print Mint distributed it until 1970, after which Denis Kitchen's Kitchen Sink Press took it over.

series.name: Bizarre Sex
series.description: Bizarre Sex was an adult underground comix anthology published by Denis Kitchen's Kitchen Sink Press, running from 1972 to 1982. Contributors over its run included Robert Crumb, Howard Cruse, Jay Lynch, Justin Green, Mike Vosburg, Peter Poplaski and Kitchen himself.

series.name: Bleeding Hearts
series.description: Bleeding Hearts is a horror series written by Deniz Camp and illustrated by Stipan Morian, published under DC's Vertigo imprint beginning in February 2026. The zombies won: ten years after the fall of humanity they are the dominant life on Earth, with their own society, language and customs. Its protagonist, a beloved member of his community known as Poke, finds his life upended the day his heart mysteriously starts beating again.

series.name: Blood of the Wolf Man
series.description: Universal Monsters: Blood of the Wolf Man is a four-issue limited series by writer Joshua Williamson and artist Leomacs, published by Skybound and Image Comics in partnership with Universal, beginning in June 2026. Set in the 1970s, it follows college student Adam Jaeger, one of the few survivors of a massacre at a party he may have caused himself, as he fights to keep the wolf from breaking free. Williamson has described it as a story about family and generational trauma.

series.name: Boy Island
series.description: Boy Island is a graphic novel by Leo Fox, published by Silver Sprocket. A modern transgender fable told in Fox's organic, surreal style, it follows Lucille, who lives on Girl Island, one of two islands formed when the world was split in twain, but who is secretly a boy.

series.name: Buzz
series.description: Buzz was a black-and-white humor anthology published by Kitchen Sink Press, beginning in August 1990. Its first issue gathered strips by Daniel Clowes, Drew Friedman, Richard Sala and Jim Woodring alongside early computer-generated art by Mark Landman and a classic George Herriman Krazy Kat reprint.

series.name: Buzzard
series.description: Buzzard was a long-running alternative comics anthology published by Cat-Head Comics, launched in 1990 and edited by Stephen Beaupre. A black-and-white magazine for mature readers, it served as a showcase for emerging alternative cartoonists of the early 1990s, with contributors including Steve Lafler, J.R. Williams, Mary Fleener, Julie Doucet and Lloyd Dangle.

series.name: Clowns
series.description: Clowns is a one-shot underground comic by Dave Geiser, published in 1972 by the San Francisco imprint Yahoo Productions. Like much of Geiser's underground work it is sexually explicit and steeped in drug and alcohol culture.

series.name: Concrete
series.description:
Concrete is a comic book series created and written by Paul Chadwick and published by Dark Horse Comics.

The character's first appearance is Dark Horse Presents #1 (July 1986). The eponymous central character is a normal man whose brain was transplanted into a large, stone body by aliens, and who lives an extraordinary life on Earth following his escape.

The Concrete series focuses on realism. Apart from the aliens (which appear only in original series issue #3, in Concrete's recounting of his origin) and Concrete's own high-tech, artificial, stone body (which includes a host of attendant abilities), there are no supernatural or science fiction elements to any stories.

The hero tries to use his body for noble endeavors, such as helping out on a family farm. Later, Concrete climbs Mount Everest, becomes involved with a group of hardline environmental militants, and reluctantly agrees to become the spokesperson of a campaign to voluntarily reduce the Earth's population.

Concrete's sexuality is addressed in the series. An artist at heart, he collects paintings of female nudes. He is embarrassed at his lack of sexual organs; this is often the subject of hurtful jokes thrown his way.

Real-world physics apply to Concrete. Examples include Concrete breaking objects by sitting on them, or Concrete being shot forward from a braking car, due to the momentum of his large body. He is constantly breaking telephones and doorknobs, and must hire an assistant, Larry Munro, because his hands are too clumsy to handle a pen.

The series makes frequent use of thought balloons, showing characters' interior thoughts and feelings.

In addition to the comic, Paul Chadwick has drawn Concrete in many paintings. Most show the character wandering in nature, perhaps looking at a flower or some other natural curiosity.

series.name: Concrete: Fragile Creature
series.description: Concrete: Fragile Creature is a four-issue Concrete miniseries written and drawn by Paul Chadwick for Dark Horse Comics. Concrete signs on to perform the stunts and practical effects for a science fiction B-picture called Rulers of the Omniverse, and finds himself carrying the production through a meddling new studio head, a fired director and an on-set accident he is blamed for. Chadwick draws on his own time in the film industry to set Concrete's humanism against the mercenary ethics of low-budget Hollywood.

series.name: Concrete: Killer Smile
series.description: Concrete: Killer Smile is a four-issue Concrete miniseries written and drawn by Paul Chadwick for Dark Horse Comics. It turns from the series' usual slice-of-life register to a thriller centered on Larry Munro, Concrete's assistant and chauffeur, who stops for a tank of gas and ends up at gunpoint, forced to drive a pyromaniac bent on burning Los Angeles to the ground. Collected as Concrete Volume 4: Killer Smile.

series.name: Concrete: Stars Over Sand
series.description: Concrete: Stars Over Sand is a five-issue miniseries written and drawn by Paul Chadwick, published by Dark Horse Comics from June 2026 and the first all-new Concrete story since 2012. Concrete has gone into the desert and not come back; Larry and Maureen are frantic as reports come in of him wandering the arid mountains covered in blood and attacking people. Lightning-struck and amnesiac, he roams a world he can no longer make sense of.

series.name: Creatures of the Id
series.description: Creatures of the Id is a one-shot anthology published by Caliber Press in October 1990, with work by Mike Allred, Jeffrey Lang and Bernie Mireault. It carries the first appearance and partial origin of Frank Einstein, who would go on to become Allred's Madman.

series.name: Criminal
series.description: Criminal is an American creator-owned comic book series written by Ed Brubaker and illustrated by Sean Phillips. It was originally published by Marvel Comics' Icon imprint and later by Image Comics. The series is a meditation on the clichés of the crime genre while remaining realistic and believable.

series.name: Criminal: Special Edition
series.description:
One-shot featuring an all-new Criminal story by Ed Brubaker & Sean Phillips. This is the first Criminal comic published by Image Comics. All the previous mini-series were published by Icon Comics, a Marvel imprint.

Collected in Criminal: Wrong Time, Wrong Place.

Note: The indicia reads "Criminal: The Special Edition (One-Shot)".

series.name: Dark Spaces: Wildfire
series.description: Dark Spaces: Wildfire is a five-issue miniseries written by Scott Snyder with art by Hayden Sherman and colors by Ronda Pattison, published by IDW Publishing in 2022 as the first Dark Spaces story. Six weeks into California's historic Arroyo Fire, Crew 513, women from an inmate firefighting program led by corrections officer Ruby "Ana" Ning, find themselves working miles from the mansion of a new recruit's crooked former associate, and have to decide whether to gamble the one clear road back to normal life on a heist under cover of smoke and ash. Collected in Dark Spaces: Wildfire.

series.name: Deadline
series.description: Deadline was a British comics magazine founded by the 2000 AD artists Brett Ewins and Steve Dillon, published from October 1988 to 1995 across 69 issues. Mixing strips with music and culture writing for adult readers, it stood alongside Crisis, Revolver and Toxic! in the wave of mature British anthologies, and its first issue carried the debut of Jamie Hewlett and Alan Martin's Tank Girl, along with the first appearances of Hugo Tate and Wired World.

series.name: Deadman
series.description:
Deadman is a thirteen-issue series written by Bruce Jones with art by John Watkiss, published by DC's Vertigo imprint from October 2006 to November 2007 and reimagining the classic character. Brandon Cayce, a cocky young airline pilot, dies when his brother Scott deliberately flies their plane into a London skyscraper, and wakes in another reality where Sarah is his wife rather than his brother's, learning that for a dead man, opening doors between dimensions has consequences for the living.

Collected Editions

- Vol. 1: Deadman Walking (#1-5)

series.name: Did You Hear About Mimi Green?
series.description: Did You Hear About Mimi Green? is a four-issue horror miniseries from Dark Horse Comics, marking the comics debut of writer Connor Goldsmith with art by Josh Cornillon and letters by Ariana Maher. Mimi Green is a polished cultural tastemaker and essayist until an old blog post surfaces with cruel remarks about fat people and the backlash goes viral. Retreating to a secluded wellness center in Topanga, she finds the sound baths and crystal healings of the day giving way at night to another, older version of the building, gilded and gluttonous, where the vainglorious are punished over and over.

series.name: Dracula: Vlad the Impaler
series.description:
This mini-series recounts the life of Vlad the Impaler and his origin as the vampire Dracula.

Collected in Dracula: Vlad the Impaler.

series.name: Eerie
series.description: Eerie is an American magazine of horror comics introduced in 1966 by Warren Publishing. Like Mad, it was a black-and-white magazine intended for newsstand distribution and did not submit its stories to the comic book industry's voluntary Comics Code Authority. Each issue's stories were introduced by the host character, Cousin Eerie. Its sister publications were Creepy and Vampirella.

series.name: Eightball
series.description: Eightball is a comic book by Daniel Clowes and published by Fantagraphics. It ran from 1989 to 2004. Eightball has been among the best-selling series in alternative comics. The series, and Clowes, were recognized with multiple industry awards, including four Eisner Awards, 14 Harvey Awards, and five Ignatz Awards.

series.name: Eros/Psyche
series.description: Eros/Psyche is a five-issue miniseries written, drawn and colored by Maria Llovet, published in English by Ablaze beginning in March 2021. The Rose is a paradise of a girls' boarding school, so long as you follow its rules; break them and you may be expelled, or worse. Sara and Silje learn its curriculum of classes by day and curses and spells by night, and the tender love that grows between them strains against the dark secret society at the school's heart.

series.name: Faithless
series.description: Faithless is a six-issue series written by Brian Azzarello and drawn by Maria Llovet, published by Boom! Studios in 2019. Faith dabbles in the occult, which her friends take for charm and she takes seriously, and she is right that there is power within reach, but she is bored as hell, and Hell has noticed. An explicit, unfiltered book about faith, sex and the devil. Collected in Faithless.

series.name: Faithless II
series.description: Faithless II is a six-issue sequel by Brian Azzarello and Maria Llovet, published by Boom! Studios in 2020. Faith takes her lovers Louis (the Devil) and his daughter Poppy to Turin, a city of fashion, art and literature that is also the reputed epicenter of black magic, and brings her steadily growing power to bear on it. Collected in Faithless II.

series.name: Fatale
series.description: Fatale is a supernatural noir comic book created by Ed Brubaker and Sean Phillips. It was published by Image Comics between January 2012 and July 2014. The series was initially announced as a 12-issue limited series, but was later extended to 24 issues.

series.name: Femme Noire
series.description: Femme Noire is a one-shot published by Cat-Head Comics in 1989, written and drawn by David A. Cherry and Shirin Tolle with a cover by Steve Lafler. It collects two stories, "The Shamness" and "Wimp Rock Babylon."

series.name: Feral
series.description: Feral is a horror series by Tony Fleecs, Trish Forstner, Tone Rodriguez and Brad Simpson, published by Image Comics from 2024 and set in the same world as the creators' Stray Dogs. Three housecats (Elsie, Lord Fluffy Britches and Patch) are lost outdoors when a rabies outbreak turns the surrounding wildlife murderous, and must find their way home through a forest of rabid beasts. The series was named an American Library Association Outstanding Comics for Young Adults honor book in 2025.

series.name: Final Cut
series.description: Final Cut is a graphic novel written and drawn by Charles Burns, published by Pantheon in September 2024. Brian, an aspiring filmmaker, takes an old 8mm camera to a remote cabin with Jimmy, Tina and Laurie to shoot a science fiction horror film in homage to Invasion of the Body Snatchers. As his feelings for Laurie go unreturned, he writes and draws himself into a fantasy in which she is muse, damsel and savior at once, and Burns lets the dream sequences and the reality bleed into an unreliable whole.

series.name: Fire and Ice: Darkwolf
series.description: Fire and Ice: Darkwolf is a five-issue miniseries written by Dan Panosian and illustrated by Andrey Lurevich, published by Dynamite Entertainment beginning in July 2026 and drawn from the world of Ralph Bakshi and Frank Frazetta's Fire and Ice. A mother flees with her twins from the warlock who sired them, until a masked warrior comes down from the mountains and falls on their pursuers.

series.name: Floating BunnyHead: Bonus Levels Collection
series.description: Floating BunnyHead and friends are a group of oddball rascals who find themselves neck-deep in trouble seemingly everywhere they go.

series.name: Frank
series.description: Frank is a cartoon character created by American cartoonist Jim Woodring. Frank is a bipedal, bucktoothed animal of uncertain species whom Woodring described as a "generic anthropomorph". The stories and supporting characters appear in a world called the Unifactor.

series.name: Geiger
series.description: Geiger is a post-apocalyptic series by writer Geoff Johns and artist Gary Frank with colorist Brad Anderson, published by Image Comics under the Ghost Machine imprint and continuing from their 2021 miniseries. Twenty-five years after a nuclear war, Tariq Geiger, the Glowing Man whose body has become a living reactor waiting to go off, walks the irradiated roads of the former United States with his two-headed wolf Barney, feared even by the Nightcrawlers and the Organ People. It anchors the shared universe of The Unnamed.

series.name: Grrl Scouts: Stone Ghost
series.description: Grrl Scouts: Stone Ghost is a six-issue miniseries written, drawn and colored by Jim Mahfood, published by Image Comics in 2021. Mahfood returns to his creator-owned Grrl Scouts universe as Dio, Turtleneck Jones and Gordi take on the sinister and unpredictable evil of the Teeth, in a psychedelic, over-the-top adventure that runs from street level out into the cosmos.

series.name: Hank Howard, Pizza Detective: A Slice of Life
series.description: Hank Howard, Pizza Detective: A Slice of Life is a two-part story from Bad Idea Comics, written by Robert Venditti and drawn by David Lapham, beginning in May 2026. Hank, the in-house detective for regional pizza chain Big Caligula's, returns to his hometown of Tampa when customer George Horvath turns up dead, and finds himself in his first homicide case: lawyers, a long-lost flame, pirates and bullets.

series.name: Harley Quinn X Elvira
series.description: Harley Quinn X Elvira is a six-issue crossover between DC and Dynamite Entertainment, written by Amanda Conner and Jimmy Palmiotti and published in 2025. A bored Harley sets out to throw the greatest Halloween street party Gotham has ever seen and decides Elvira should host it; Elvira, whose show has just been axed by the suits, needs a new gig. Their meeting leads to pie, partnership and disaster for anyone in their way.

series.name: Harrow County
series.description: Harrow County is an American comic book series that ran from 2015 to 2018. It was created by writer Cullen Bunn and artist Tyler Crook, and published by Dark Horse Comics.

series.name: Heart Eyes
series.description: Sanity-eating monsters ended humanity. The unlucky few who survived now hide in the cracks of a broken world. And yet somehow, beneath the graveyard that used to be San Antonio, Rico met Lupe, the girl of his dreams. But how did she get here? And why is she smiling? No one survives out in the street. No one smiles where the monsters lurk.

series.name: Heavy Liquid
series.description: Heavy Liquid is a five-issue limited series written and drawn by Paul Pope, published by DC's Vertigo imprint between October 1999 and February 2000. In a New York and Paris of roughly 2075, a former cop known only as S works as a finder of people and things, and is himself addicted to heavy liquid, a substance a wealthy collector wants cast as sculpture, a crew of masked gunmen want as an explosive, and a government agency wants out of circulation altogether. Hired to track down the one artist who can shape the stuff, S crosses two continents against psychopaths and his own habit. Collected in Heavy Liquid.

series.name: Heavy Metal
series.description:
Heavy Metal is an American science fantasy comics magazine, first published in 1977. The magazine is known primarily for its blend of dark fantasy, science fiction, erotica, and steampunk comics. Following a brief hiatus in 2023, it relaunched in 2024 with new owners and a new editorial team consisting of Dave Kelly, Frank Forte, and Chris Thompson.

Unlike the traditional American comic books of that time bound by the restrictive Comics Code Authority, the magazine-format Heavy Metal featured explicit nudity, sexual situations, and graphic violence. The magazine started out primarily as a licensed translation of the French science-fantasy magazine Métal hurlant, marking for many Americans their first introduction to the work of European cartoonists like Enki Bilal, Philippe Caza, Guido Crepax, Philippe Druillet, Jean-Claude Forest, Jean Giraud (a.k.a. Moebius), Chantal Montellier, and Milo Manara.

series.name: Hup
series.description: Hup is a solo comic book by Robert Crumb, published by Last Gasp across four issues between 1987 and 1992. Drawn from 1986 onward, it returned Crumb to Mr. Natural and Flakey Foont after a decade away, and introduced Devil Girl; its best-known strip, "The Ruff-Tuff Cream-Puffs Take Charge!", follows a gang fed up with liberal wimps taking over the U.S.A.

series.name: Hyde Street
series.description: Hyde Street is a horror series by writer Geoff Johns and artist Ivan Reis, published by Image Comics under the Ghost Machine imprint from October 2024. Take a wrong turn in any town and you may find yourself on Hyde Street, where the consequences of who you talk to and what you do make death look like the easy way out. Part Twilight Zone anthology and part ongoing mystery, it follows a cast of sinister Residents, among them the cynical ad man Mr. X-Ray and the evil boy scout Pranky, along with the tormented souls who bargain with them.

series.name: Ice Cream Man
series.description: Ice Cream Man is a semi-anthological horror series written by W. Maxwell Prince and drawn by Martin Morazzo with colorist Chris O'Halloran, published by Image Comics from 2018. Each issue is a largely standalone tale of sorrow, wonder and dread with its own cast and its own formal conceit, so that any issue can be a reader's first. Running faintly beneath them all is the story of Riccardus, the demented cosmic thing who drives the ice cream truck, and his centuries-long feud with his nemesis Caleb.

series.name: If Destruction Be Our Lot
series.description: If Destruction Be Our Lot is a science fiction series written by Mark Elijah Rosenberg and Matthew Rosenberg with art by Andy MacDonald, colors by Francesco Segala and letters by Hassan Otsmane-Elhaou, published by Image Comics from May 2026. Humanity is extinct and robots run the world; a lonely Abraham Lincoln android named Abe, convinced there must be something more out there, sets out to wander the Earth and find it, or get recycled trying.

series.name: Infernal Hulk
series.description: Infernal Hulk is a Marvel series written by Phillip Kennedy Johnson and drawn by Nic Klein. The evil called the Eldest has torn Bruce Banner and the Hulk apart and taken the Hulk's body for itself, producing a monster ten times worse than the one anyone feared, bent on dragging the world back into ancient horrors by turning Marvel's heroes into beasts, while a powerless Banner works to stop it. The series leads into the Hulk War crossover. Cover title "The Infernal Hulk"; indicia title "Infernal Hulk".

series.name: It’s Jeff: Brand New Week
series.description: It's Jeff: Brand New Week is a Marvel one-shot released in June 2026, written by Kelly Thompson with art by Gurihiru, Goodman Yamada and Irene Strychalski. Jeff the Land Shark takes up with a clingy septapus named Ken, an octopus with only seven arms, in a 40-page collection that gathers Jeff Week material along with early Jeff appearances opposite Deadpool and Elsa Bloodstone.

series.name: Jacked
series.description: Jacked is a six-issue miniseries written by Eric Kripke, the creator of Supernatural, with art by John Higgins and covers by Glenn Fabry, published by DC's Vertigo imprint in 2015-16. Josh Jaffe, a neurotic family man deep in a midlife slump, orders a smart pill online to sharpen his focus and finds it gives him enormous strength instead, and that it is savagely addictive. Collected in Jacked.

series.name: Juice City
series.description: Juice City is an underground comix magazine published by Tucker Petertil, its first issue cover-dated Winter 1977-1978. The magazine-sized anthology carried work by George Metzger, Hunt Emerson, Doug Hansen and Doug Bryson.

series.name: Just Brutal
series.description: Just Brutal is a series written by Dennis Hopeless with art by Brahm Revel and colors by Marissa Louise, published by Ignition Press from February 2026. The Savage twins learn their parents are eternal warriors who have spent their immortality defending Earth from the warlord Farklar the Fleshless, and are dragged onto a family road trip to stop his latest scheme. The book plays its monsters against family and mental health.

series.name: King Spawn
series.description: King Spawn is an ongoing series launched by Image Comics in August 2021 as part of Todd McFarlane's expanded Spawn's Universe, written by Sean Lewis with McFarlane and drawn by Javi Fernández. Picking up from Spawn's Universe #1, it sets Spawn against a classic enemy from his past who has returned to Earth to corrupt as many souls as he can, and whose existence only Spawn suspects. Its debut issue was the best-selling comic of 2021.

series.name: Kingdom Of Earth
series.description:
From the critically acclaimed writing duo of David Dastmalchian and Leah Kilpatrick and the Bram Stoker Award–winning artist Soo Lee comes this all-new monstrous miniseries.

• Co-written by actor, writer, and producer David Dastmalchian and Leah Kilpatrick!

• In the vein of Sweet Tooth, The Mandalorian, and The Last of Us.

series.name: Lady Killer
series.description: Lady Killer is a 2015-2016 comic book series written by Joëlle Jones and Jamie S. Rich, illustrated by Joëlle Jones and colored by Laura Allred. The comic is a thriller taking place in the 1960s, and tells the story of Josie Schuller, a perfect housewife who leads a secret life as killer-for-hire in her spare time.

series.name: Legion of Super-Heroes
series.description:
Starring: Legion of Super-Heroes.

Continued from: Legion of Super-Heroes (Volume 3)

Runs in tandem with: Legionnaires (Starting in 1993).

series.name: Lobo
series.description: Lobo is the Czarnian bounty hunter's second and longest-running solo series, published by DC Comics for 64 issues between 1993 and 1999 plus two specials. Written by Alan Grant with art by Val Semeiks and John Dell, it dropped the mature-readers label of the earlier miniseries and ran as a monthly frag-fest of gratuitous violence and blackly comic excess.

series.name: Love and Rockets
series.description:
Love and Rockets (often abbreviated L&R) is a comic book series by the Hernandez brothers: Gilbert, Jaime, and Mario. It was one of the first comic books in the alternative comics movement of the 1980s.

The Hernandez brothers produce stories in the series independently of each other. Gilbert and Jaime produce the majority of the material, and tend to focus on particular casts of characters and settings. Those of Gilbert usually focus on a cast of characters in the fictional Central American village of Palomar; the stories often feature magic realist elements. The Locas stories of Jaime center on a social group in Los Angeles, particularly the Latina friends and sometime-lovers Maggie and Hopey.

series.name: Madman
series.description: Madman is a creator-owned fictional superhero that appears in comic books by creator Mike Allred and which has been published by a number of publishers over the years. The character first appeared in Creatures of the Id #1 (Oct. 1990). His name, Frank Einstein, is a combination of Frank Sinatra and Albert Einstein, and is also a reference to Frankenstein.

series.name: Madman Adventures
series.description: Madman Adventures is a three-issue miniseries written and drawn by Mike Allred, published by Tundra in 1993 and the first Madman series in color. It runs from a day in the life of Frank Einstein through a trip back into prehistory and a closing dream, and was preceded by an ashcan edition issued as Hero Premiere Edition #4.

series.name: Madman Picture Exhibition
series.description: In April of 1992 the very first issue of Madman was unleashed into the comic book universe. In celebration of 10 years of Madman, AAA POP Comics presents the greatest collection of Comic book artists and illustrators on a single project ever! It's a humble claim that defies any challenge given the talent involved. This series of Madman masterpieces is a list of simply the best, most inspirational, most legendary, and finest artists that have ever graced the comic book medium.

series.name: Mickey Rat
series.description:
Mickey Rat is an underground comix title by Robert Armstrong, an unmistakable parody of Mickey Mouse billed on its first cover as the Potentate of Puke. Armstrong drew the character for a T-shirt in 1971 and debuted him in L.A. Comics #1 that December, with early stories scripted by Chester C. Crill; four issues appeared between 1972 and 1982.

#1 published by Los Angeles Comic Book Company

#2 published by Kitchen Sink

3-4 published by Last Gasp

series.name: Mind MGMT: New & Improved
series.description: Mind MGMT: New & Improved is a series written, drawn, colored and designed by Matt Kindt, published by Oni Press from June 2026 as the launch title of his Flux House imprint. The agents who survived the extra-governmental agency are living quiet, fabricated lives underground until someone begins hunting them with methods that read less like murder than a conceptual art project involving neurotoxins, trains and dismemberment, and Detectives Delphi and Swan start pulling at the threads. It is built as a self-contained entry point into the Eisner-nominated series.

series.name: Minor Arcana
series.description: Minor Arcana is a supernatural series written and drawn by Jeff Lemire, published by Boom! Studios from September 2024 and his first creator-owned ongoing for the publisher. Theresa, daughter of a small-town psychic and tarot-reading fraud, comes home to care for her dying mother and finds a town seemingly untouched by time, more truth in her mother's magic than she expected, and the beginnings of real ability in herself. Its four arcs mirror the suits of the tarot: The Book of Wands, of Swords, of Cups and of Pentacles.

series.name: Motor City Comics
series.description: Motor City Comics is an underground comix title written and drawn by Robert Crumb and published by Rip Off Press, beginning in April 1969. Its two issues introduced Lenore Goldberg and her Girl Commandos alongside strips including "Deep Meaning Comics," "The Desperate Character" and "The Inimitable Boingy Baxter."

series.name: My Body is Unspooling
series.description: My Body Is Unspooling is a minicomic by the UK cartoonist and painter Leo Fox, published by Silver Sprocket in 2024. It follows Lucille, whose body and mind are permanently at odds: Lucille too cold and too resentful for his body, his body too warm and too loud for Lucille. The comic worries at what holds the two together.

series.name: Nut
series.description: A surreal self-published comic book about agency, purpose, and love.

series.name: Odin
series.description:
Green Room meets Midsommar in JAMES TYNION’s most relentless Horror story yet! Adela will do anything for the perfect story. Including going undercover with Neo Nazi punks headed to the frozen forests of Norway under the misbegotten belief that they can summon Odin and achieve their promised white destiny. But what awaits them in the woods is far older and stranger than any of them can comprehend. And no gods are coming to answer their prayers for help.

Multiple Eisner Award-winning creator JAMES TYNION IV (Exquisite Corpses), no-holds-barred writer MARGUERITE BENNETT (Witchblade), rising star artist LETIZIA CADONICI (House of Slaughter), and Eisner Award-winning colorist JORDIE BELLAIRE (Redlands) conjure a hallucinogenic horror story that leaves absolutely no taboo unbroken.

series.name: Omaha
series.description:
"Omaha" the Cat Dancer is an erotic comic strip and later comic book created by artist Reed Waller and writer Kate Worley. Set in fictional Mipple City, Minnesota (derived from "MPLS", the old postal abbreviation for Minneapolis) in a universe populated by anthropomorphic animal characters, the strip is a soap opera focusing on Omaha, a feline exotic dancer, and her lover, Chuck, the son of a business tycoon.

The strip debuted in the funny animal magazine Vootie, and it was subsequently published in a number of underground comix in the late 1970s and early 1980s. "Omaha" the Cat Dancer became the subject of the eponymous comic book series published from 1984 to 1993 by Kitchen Sink Press; it was relaunched by Fantagraphics Books through 1995. The final chapters of the strip's storyline were published in Sizzle magazine, beginning in 2006.

"Omaha" the Cat Dancer was the first of several comic books published in the early 1980s which integrated explicit sex into their storylines, rather than using sex for shock value. The comic was the subject of a number of obscenity controversies, and it was nominated for multiple Eisner Awards in 1989 and 1991.

series.name: Pacific Presents
series.description: Pacific Presents was an anthology title from the independent publisher Pacific Comics, beginning in October 1982. Its first two issues carried the third and fourth chapters of Dave Stevens' The Rocketeer, picking up from Starslayer #2-3, alongside Steve Ditko's Missing Man; in the second Cliff Secord meets a pair of familiar-looking gentlemen who turn out to work for Doc Savage.

series.name: Panic
series.description: Panic was a bi-monthly humor comic published by Bill Gaines' EC Comics, running twelve issues from February 1954. Edited by Al Feldstein and billed by EC as the "only authorized imitation" of Harvey Kurtzman's Mad (a joke Kurtzman did not enjoy), it ran parodies of film, television and literature drawn by Jack Davis, Will Elder, Jack Kamen, Joe Orlando, Basil Wolverton and Wally Wood.

series.name: People's Comics
series.description: The People's Comics is a one-shot underground comic written and drawn almost entirely by Robert Crumb, published in September 1972 by Terry Zwigoff's Golden Gate Publishing Company, with a back-cover feature by a young Harvey Pekar. It is best known for containing the death of Fritz the Cat, Crumb's response to his disappointment with Ralph Bakshi's 1972 film. Zwigoff soon sold the printing rights to Kitchen Sink Press, which issued the following six printings.

series.name: Red Book
series.description: Red Book is a four-issue miniseries written by James Tynion IV, drawn by Michael Avon Oeming and colored by Brian Level, published by Dark Horse Comics from October 2025 as a continuation of Blue Book. It turns the series' true-weird approach on UFO history behind the Iron Curtain in the Soviet Union and China, opening in Russia in 1961 with the nine students who died in the Dyatlov Pass incident.

series.name: Red Roots
series.description: Red Roots is a supernatural mystery written and drawn by Lorenzo De Felici, published by Image Comics from April 2026 and his debut as a writer. A professional killer and a high school teacher find their lives bound together by a terrifying, unexplained force, and each chapter pushes further into the dark fantasy lore behind it.

series.name: Redcoat
series.description: Redcoat is a series created by Geoff Johns and Bryan Hitch with colorist Brad Anderson and letterer Rob Leigh, published by Image Comics under the Ghost Machine imprint from April 2024. Simon Pure, a British deserter in the American Revolution, blunders into immortality after an encounter with the Founding Fathers (a secret order counting George Washington and John Hancock among its members), and centuries later has to face his own cowardice and a plot to destroy the country he ran from. A feature film adaptation is in development at Atlas Entertainment with Johns writing.

series.name: Rip Off Comix
series.description: Rip Off Comix was an underground comix anthology published by Rip Off Press from April 1977 to 1991, running bi-annually in comic-book format until 1983 and quarterly in magazine format from 1987. It began as a byproduct of the Rip Off Press syndication service, which sold weekly strips to alternative newspapers and student papers, and carried new Fabulous Furry Freak Brothers and Wonder Wart-Hog material by Gilbert Shelton and Paul Mavrides alongside work by Frank Stack, Ted Richards, Dave Sheridan, Bill Griffith and Justin Green.

series.name: Seamonsters and Superheroes
series.description: Seamonsters and Superheroes is an eight-issue series written and drawn by the Ignatz Award-winning cartoonist Scott Mills, published in black and white by SLG Publishing beginning in 2003. Its short pieces range from sea monsters and superheroes to slice-of-life vignettes and stray observations; the run was collected as a trade paperback in March 2005.

series.name: Silver Surfer Annual
series.description:
Starting in 1988, the Silver Surfer Annual accompanied Silver Surfer Vol. 3. It lasted for 7 issues from 1988 till 1994, although the main series lasted until 1998. Annuals were not published for 1995-1996. In 1997 the annuals were titled with a unique indica;

- Silver Surfer '97 - Silver Surfer / Thor '98

series.name: Skinbreaker
series.description: Skinbreaker is an eight-issue series written by Robert Kirkman and drawn by David Finch, with colorist Annalisa Leoni and letterer Rus Wooton, published by Image Comics from September 2025. Enor has led his tribe for many seasons but can barely lift the mighty Skinbreaker any more, and as a bloody succession struggle opens between him and his reluctant heir Anok, a far larger threat waits in the dark beyond the village.

series.name: Snarf
series.description: Snarf was an underground humor anthology published by Denis Kitchen's Kitchen Sink Press, launched in February 1972 alongside the company's Bizarre Sex and Death Rattle. Contributors included Tim Boxell, Jay Lynch, Justin Green, Howard Cruse, Joel Beck, Richard "Grass" Green, Peter Poplaski, Evert Geradts, George Metzger and Kitchen himself; one early issue scored a front cover from Will Eisner featuring the Spirit.

series.name: Space Riders
series.description: Space Riders is a four-issue miniseries written by Fabian Rangel Jr. and drawn by Alexis Ziritt, published by Black Mask Studios in 2015. Capitán Peligro and the crew of the skullship Santa Muerte (the android Yara and the spiritual warrior Mono) deal harsh justice to the scum of the galaxy while hunting the hidden truths of the universe, in a psychedelic, brutally colored take on space opera. Collected as Space Riders: Vengeful Universe.

series.name: Space Riders: Galaxy of Brutality
series.description: Space Riders: Galaxy of Brutality is a four-issue miniseries by writer Fabian Rangel Jr. and artist Alexis Ziritt, published by Black Mask Studios in 2017 and the second Space Riders series. Capitán Peligro, Yara and Mono return to the skullship Santa Muerte and take on cosmic biker gangs and a destroyer god with designs on the universe. Collected as Space Riders: Galaxy of Brutality.

series.name: Space Riders: Vortex of Darkness
series.description: Space Riders: Vortex of Darkness is a four-issue miniseries written by Carlos Giffoni with art by Alexis Ziritt, published by Black Mask Studios in 2019 and the third Space Riders series. Twenty years after the riders killed the Destroyer God of Evil, the Mother of All Evil Gods rises to claim every dimension and every possible reality, and the now cybernetically enhanced ex-riders reunite for a suicide run into her mind to assassinate her soul. Collected as Space Riders Vol. 3: Vortex of Darkness.

series.name: Stray Bullets
series.description:
Stray Bullets is an independent American comic book series published in black and white (with color covers) by El Capitan Books and Image Comics. It is written and drawn by David Lapham.

The story deals with the often criminal and sometimes tragic misadventures of a large cast of characters and takes place from the mid-1970s through the mid-1990s. Published on an irregular basis since 1995, the comic has had close to 100 issues and is a long-time critically acclaimed series.

series.name: Stray Bullets: Sunshine & Roses
series.description: Third volume of Stray Bullets. Continues from Stray Bullets: The Killers.Collected EditionsStray Bullets: Sunshine & Roses Part 1 - Kretchmeyer (#1-8)Stray Bullets: Sunshine & Roses Part 2 - Change of Plans (#9-16)Stray Bullets: Sunshine & Roses Part 3 - The Queen of Palm Court (#17-24)Stray Bullets: Sunshine & Roses Part 4 - The Salad Days (#25-32)Note: Volume named per the indicia which uses the ampersand.

series.name: Street Poet Ray
series.description: Street Poet Ray is a four-issue black-and-white series published bi-monthly by Marvel's Epic imprint from April to October 1990, written by Michael Redmond with art by Junko Hosizawa. Each issue collects short verses by Ray, a street poet who makes his living reciting them, on subjects from the Red Cross to the plight of working mothers, set against plainly drawn scenes of city life. The back of each issue carried a 900 number readers could call for Ray's rap of the day.

series.name: Tales Calculated to Drive You Mad
series.description: Tales Calculated to Drive You Mad was an eight-issue series published by E.C. Publications between 1997 and 1999, reprinting in full color the first twenty-three comic-book-format issues of Mad, covers included. Issued roughly three times a year, it opened with Harvey Kurtzman's Mad #1-3 and the parodies of the Lone Ranger, Tarzan, Dragnet, Robin Hood, Batman, Sherlock Holmes and Wonder Woman drawn by Kurtzman, Wally Wood, Jack Davis, Will Elder and John Severin.

series.name: Tales of Ordinary Madness
series.description: Tales of Ordinary Madness is a four-issue black-and-white miniseries written by Malcolm Bourne and drawn by Mike Allred, with covers by John Bolton, published by Dark Horse Comics in 1992. Loosely linked case studies bring patients with violent mental illnesses to the door of a psychiatrist who is not entirely well himself: Robert, convinced he is watched wherever he goes; Jane Brown and her depression; David Wolff, found walking in traffic. The Doctor is by turns sympathetic, callous and sinister as he slides toward his own breakdown. The book is unusually gritty, formally experimental early work from Allred.

series.name: Tasty Comix
series.description: Tasty Comix is a one-shot underground comix anthology published around 1969-1970 by the Washington Free Community, the collective behind the Washington Free Press. Its 36 pages collect work by cartoonists from the Washington, D.C. underground scene, among them Gregory Kwater, Patrick Burk, Tom Howell, Bill Fairfax, Al Simons and Sherry Ives, alongside a contribution from Skip Williamson.

series.name: The Beauty
series.description: The Beauty is a creator-owned series written by Jeremy Haun and Jason A. Hurley with art by Haun, launched at Image Comics in August 2015 after winning Top Cow's Pilot Season in 2011. The Beauty is a sexually transmitted disease that makes you gorgeous: fat melts away, hair thickens, features slim. Two years into the craze, more than half of America has caught it deliberately. Detectives Kara Vaughn, herself infected, and Foster work the first deaths and fall into the conspiracies keeping the disease on the market.

series.name: The City Beneath Her Feet
series.description: The City Beneath Her Feet is a series by writer James Tynion IV and artist Elsa Charretier, published by DSTLRY from 2024 and pitched as a grindhouse thriller and love story. Jasper Jayne was the girl of Zara's dreams, gone as fast as she arrived; years later Zara finds herself listed as Jasper's emergency contact, piecing together who Jasper really was while the assassins who once counted her one of their own close in.

series.name: The Deadman
series.description: The Deadman is a series written by W. Maxwell Prince and drawn by Martin Morazzo, published by DC Comics from 2026 as part of its Next Level initiative. In the wake of DC K.O. the balance between life and death has collapsed, leaving souls stuck in a loop of ghostly derangement; Boston Brand, remade as a Spiritual Custodian working for Rama Kushna, patrols an Earth-bound purgatory and ushers the dead into the Great Whereafter under the Laws of Sacred Math, until a demonic threat to the balance forces him back into the suit. Solicited as a six-issue limited series, it was extended through issue #12.

series.name: The Dogsitter
series.description: The Dogsitter is a romance series by writer Jamie S. Rich and artist Megan Levens, the collaborators behind Ares & Aphrodite and Madame Frankenstein, published by Ignition Press from June 2026. Gemma Monroe has taken a leave from veterinary school to save for tuition, stacking shifts at a flower shop and dogsitting on the side; her favorite client, an Akita with an identity crisis, comes attached to Portia Ross, a high-powered executive who treats Gemma as a pet project of her own. Then Gemma meets the charming Neal Mandell, and a casual fling turns into a transactional triangle that could cost her the future she is working toward.

series.name: The Eye Collector
series.description: The Eye Collector is a five-issue horror series published in 2021 by VIRUS, the creator-owned imprint of Heavy Metal. Nathan tries to shield the people he loves from a figure stitched together out of the Sandman and the Man in the Moon: the Eye Collector grants mortals whatever they most desire, and takes their eyes in payment to fuel his magic.

series.name: The Many Deaths of Laila Starr
series.description: The Many Deaths of Laila Starr is a five-issue miniseries written by Ram V and drawn by Filipe Andrade, published by Boom! Studios from April 2021 and set in Ram V's native Mumbai. With humanity on the verge of inventing immortality, the avatar of Death is made redundant and cast down into the mortal body of a twenty-something named Laila Starr, who lands, by arrangement, in the time and place where the child who will end death is about to be born. Collected in The Many Deaths of Laila Starr.

series.name: The Maxx
series.description:
The Maxx is an American comic book series created by Sam Kieth in 1993 and originally published monthly until 1998 by Image Comics for 35 issues, before being collected in trade paperback by DC Comics' Wildstorm imprint. The first appearance of the titular character was in Darker Image #1 by Image Comics in March 1993. The comic book, starring an eponymous purple-clad hero, spawned a 13-episode animated series on MTV that originally aired April–June 1995. Starting in November 2013 and ending in September 2016, the original series has been republished by IDW as The Maxx: Maxximized with new colors and improved scans of the original artwork by Sam Kieth and Jim Sinclair. In 2018, the Maxx featured in a five-issue crossover series with Batman, published by IDW.

The series follows the adventures of the titular hero in two worlds: the real world and an alternate reality referred to as the Outback. In the real world, Maxx is a vagrant, a "homeless man living in a box", while in the Outback, he is the powerful protector of the Leopard Queen, who exists in the real world as Julie Winters, a freelance social worker who often bails Maxx out of jail. While Maxx is aware of the Outback, Julie is not, though it is integral to both of their stories.

series.name: The Muppets Noir
series.description: The Muppets Noir is a series written and drawn by Roger Langridge, who previously wrote The Muppet Show Comic Book, published by Dynamite Entertainment from February 2026. Frazzled by the usual pre-curtain chaos at the Muppet Theatre, Kermit settles down with a favorite old detective novel and takes a stray brick to the head. While the rest of the troupe tries to bring him round backstage, Kermit walks the streets of Dreamland as Flip Minnow, P.I., hard-boiled and with no time for song and dance until he cracks the case of the Snoozing Sleuth.

series.name: The Nice House by the Sea
series.description:
The Nice House on the Lake and The Nice House by the Sea are two post-apocalyptic horror comic book limited series created by writer James Tynion IV and artist Álvaro Martínez Bueno, and published by DC Comics through their Black Label imprint and since 2024, their Vertigo imprint. 

The Nice House on the Lake debuted on June 1, 2021, and concluded on December 27, 2022. This first series focuses on the mysterious Walter, who invites ten of his friends to an idyllic house in the countryside, only for them to witness the end of the world and be told they are not allowed to leave. The series received critical acclaim, winning four Eisner Awards including the 2022 award for Best New Series.

A second "cycle" in the same setting, The Nice House by the Sea, began on July 24, 2024. This series follows a different household consisting of exemplary humans selected by Max, another member of Walter's species. In October 2024, DC relaunched their Vertigo imprint and began publishing some Black Label titles, including The Nice House by the Sea, as Vertigo titles.

series.name: The Oddball's Odyssey
series.description: The Oddball's Odyssey is a 56-page one-shot written and drawn by Tony Millionaire with colors by Jim Campbell, published by Bad Idea Comics in April 2026. It runs Homer through the intricate line and open skies of Moebius's Arzach: Bobby Dougherty, a booze-hound monkey delivered into sobriety by divine providence, falls drunk on love instead for a radiant swan named Lucia Serena DelMar, and when she takes wing he and his friend Jimmy Skunk set out after her.

series.name: The Shaolin Cowboy: Staying A.I. Live
series.description: The Shaolin Cowboy: Staying A.I. Live is a four-issue miniseries written and drawn by Geof Darrow with colorist Ian Herring and letterer Nate Piekos, published by Dark Horse Comics from July 2026. The fifth Shaolin Cowboy series, it takes the character out of his wasteland retreat on an errand of mercy and strands him in a small American town where euthanasia has become the new duty on foreign imports.

series.name: The Twilight Zone
series.description: Return to the Twilight Zone in this all-new anthology series featuring stories by some of the best creators in comics today! Each issue is a new tale in the vein of the iconic original television series that’s captivated audiences for over 60 years. And like the show, these stories will be revealed in terrifying black and white!

series.name: Thrillogy
series.description: Thrillogy is a one-shot published by Pacific Comics in January 1984, collecting three full-color tales written and drawn by Tim Conrad. "Prometheus Primeval" follows a Cro-Magnon man's first glimmer of self-awareness in a savage world; "All That Glitters..." puts a young magician's apprentice onto a sinister plot; and "Red Rover, Red Rover" follows colonists trying to make a home of Mars.

series.name: Thump'n Guts
series.description: Thump'n Guts is a one-shot by Kevin Eastman and Simon Bisley, published by Kitchen Sink Press in 1993 and sold bagged as Project-X. Frustrated by the variant-chasing market of the day, the pair set out to make a deliberate "true collectible": three covers, three different endings, six trading cards and a print run capped at 100,000. The story is straight monster-fighting: something is loosed from the Earth's core, and only more monsters can force it back down.

series.name: Trencher
series.description: Trencher is a four-issue series created, written and drawn by Keith Giffen, published by Image Comics in 1993. Gideon Trencher is a zombie-like enforcer sent to exterminate souls that have been wrongfully reincarnated, guided by Phoebe, the dispatcher's voice in his head who feeds him targets and serves as his only company. Giffen drew it in a twisted ligne claire loaded with Darrow-scale detail, and pitched the whole ultraviolent thing as a parody of the prevailing Image house style.

series.name: Trumpzilla
series.description: Trumpzilla is a 32-page one-shot by the underground cartoonist Sandez Rey, self-published through IndyPlanet. Trumpzilla rises to fight a giant robot piloted by a female mad scientist, and a back-up strip follows Dr. Spiral, a lucha libre enforcer for the Catholic Church, against a werewolf.

series.name: Uneeda Comix
series.description: Uneeda Comix is an all-Crumb one-shot underground comic published by the Print Mint in 1970, with Robert Crumb responsible for the wraparound cover and every page inside. Its 28 pages run through Mr. Natural, Flakey Foont, Shuman the Human, Bo Bo Bolinski, Honeybunch Kaminski, the Simp and the Gimp and Dora Zockman, plus Don Dohler's Projunior. Five printings appeared through 1973, all with identical covers.

series.name: Universal Monsters: Phantom of the Opera
series.description: Universal Monsters: Phantom of the Opera is a four-issue limited series by writer Tyler Boss and artist Martin Simmonds, published by Skybound and Image Comics from February 2026. A run of violent crimes throws the Paris Opera House into chaos and wrecks Christine Dubois's career, and she comes to learn that no one there is what they seem, least of all the voice whispering from the eaves.

series.name: Universal Monsters: The Invisible Man
series.description: Universal Monsters: The Invisible Man is a four-issue limited series by writer James Tynion IV and artist DANI with colorist Brad Simpson, published by Skybound and Image Comics from August 2025. Jack Griffin has always felt invisible to the people around him; when an experimental breakthrough offers to make it literal, nobody, not even the woman he loves, will be allowed to stand in the way. It follows Skybound's Universal Monsters series on Dracula, Frankenstein, the Mummy and the Creature from the Black Lagoon.

series.name: W0rldtr33
series.description: W0rldtr33 is a horror series by writer James Tynion IV and artist Fernando Blanco, with colorist Jordie Bellaire and letterer Aditya Bidikar, published by Image Comics from April 2023. In 1999 Gabriel, Amanda, Liam, Yoshi and Darren found the Undernet, a secret architecture beneath the internet, and charted it on a private message board called W0rldtr33 until someone broke in who welcomed what the Undernet did to them. They believed they had sealed it away at great personal cost; they were wrong, and PH34R is watching.

series.name: Walkie Talkie
series.description:
Nate Powell's self-published solo series, four issues released through his Food Chain imprint between May 2000 and June 2002. He funded the first issue with the Shakespeare & Company Books Self-Publishing Grant, awarded when he graduated from the School of Visual Arts in 2000. Saddle-stitched, with a colour cover over black-and-white interiors.

Its stories, drawn from the complications and disappointments of young adulthood, were later collected in Tiny Giants (Soft Skull Press, 2003) and Sounds of Your Name (Microcosm Publishing, 2006).

series.name: Weirdo
series.description: Weirdo was a magazine-sized comics anthology founded by Robert Crumb and published by Last Gasp for 28 issues between 1981 and 1993. Crumb edited the first ten issues, Peter Bagge took over for #11-17 and #25, and Aline Kominsky-Crumb ran #18-24 and #26-28; the three tenures are known as Personal Confessions, the Coming of the Bad Boys, and Twisted Sisters. Deliberately low-art against the highbrow Raw, it carried work by Peter Bagge, Charles Burns, Daniel Clowes, Kim Deitch, Julie Doucet, Drew Friedman, Phoebe Gloeckner, Dori Seda, Spain Rodriguez and many others, with a Crumb cover or strip in every issue.

series.name: White Boat
series.description: White Boat is a three-issue oversized series by writer Scott Snyder and artist Francesco Francavilla, published by DSTLRY from May 2024. Nautical journalist Lee Derry accepts an invitation aboard one of the mega-yachts the super-rich use to cross the world, and finds a labyrinth of a hull and a crew carrying him toward a remote island where a cult has spent millennia at work on something called the Human Project, a cabal with deeper ties to his own history than he knows.

series.name: XYZ Comics
series.description: XYZ Comics is a one-shot underground comic written and drawn by Robert Crumb, first published by Kitchen Sink in June 1972 and reprinted several times since. It collects "Cubist Be Bop Comics," "Comical Comics," "The Many Faces of R. Crumb" and "Nut Factory Blues."

series.name: Zap Comix
series.description:
Zap Comix is an underground comix series which was originally part of the counterculture of the late 1960s. While a few small-circulation self-published satirical comic books had been printed prior to this, Zap became the model for the "comix" movement that snowballed after its release. The title itself published 17 issues over a period of 46 years.

Premiering in early 1968 as a showcase for the work of Robert Crumb, Zap was unlike any comic book that had been seen before. While working on Zap #1, Crumb saw a Family Dog poster drawn by Rick Griffin which resembled a psychedelic version of a Sunday funnies page. Its surreal, other-worldly imagery inspired him to think about comics in a new way, as seen in the art style of Zap #1's Abstract Expressionist Ultra Super Modernistic Comics. When Crumb started planning the next issue, he got in touch with Griffin, asking him to contribute to Zap #2. Griffin agreed and suggested bringing fellow poster artist Victor Moscoso on board. S. Clay Wilson, Gilbert Shelton, Robert Williams, and "Spain" Rodriguez were also contributors to Zap.

While the origin of the spelling "comix" is a subject of some dispute, it was popularized by its appearance in the title of the first issues of Zap. Design critic Steven Heller claims that the term "comix" ("co-mix") refers to the traditional comic book style of Zap, and its mixture of dirty jokes and storylines.
